title: Duchy of Sandomierz
capsule: The Duchy of Sandomierz was a Piast principality in the upper Vistula basin created by the fragmentation of the Polish kingdom under Bolesław III Wrymouth's 1138 testament, which divided Poland among his sons and established the senior principle (princeps) centred initially on Krakow and Sandomierz. It occupied the fertile Lesser Poland territory east of Krakow and was contested among rival Piast branches throughout the period of fragmentation. Duke Leszek II the Black reunited Sandomierz with Krakow in 1279, and the duchy was definitively incorporated into the reunified Kingdom of Poland when Władysław I Elbow-high was crowned king in 1320.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory is well identified from Piast documents; precise borders with neighboring duchies shifted repeatedly and are reconstructed from limited documentary evidence.
